description: Stage 3, Gate 3a: a structured trace of every turn, and open threads as first-class objects. This is the data layer everything else (predictor, sleep replay, self-build) needs to exist before it can be trusted, and it directly targets the tangent-handling failure: every unfinished thought in a message becomes a tracked object instead of being dropped.

userStories.title: Every turn writes a structured trace record
userStories.description: On every real conversation turn (the production CognitiveTurnResult path, not a test harness), write one JSON record: raw input, memories retrieved, any predictions made, the assembled prompt sections, the model output, and per-stage latency (embed/retrieve/prompt-build/generate/post-process). This is pure logging — no new behavior, no model changes.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: a trace record is written for every turn that goes through the real production entry point, not a mock/test-only path
AC2: record includes input text, retrieved memory IDs, prompt section boundaries, output text, and stage timings in milliseconds
AC3: traces are stored locally, append-only, with a replay_turn(id) function that can re-run a past turn's stored input against current logic
AC4: no PII leaves the device — this is a local file/DB, not a network call
AC5: negative control: if trace writing is disabled, a test asserts the trace file does not grow — proves the wiring is real, not a stub
userStories.notes: AC1: every real turn through the production entry writes exactly one record — proven through the REAL JVM-executable composition root TermuxJarvisServer(port=0, backendOverride=FakeModelBackend(), turnTraceStore=JsonlTurnTraceStore(tempfile)) driven through the REAL LatencyPipeline.onUserInput -> CognitiveEngine.process(sendBlock=bridgeSend) call path (the /api/chat production chain); the ONLY swapped hop is the last one (recording collector instead of modelManager.send) — the store itself is a real file. 2 pipeline turns -> exactly 2 records, each carrying the exact raw input (TurnTraceProductionWiringTest). AC2: store-level round trip proves every field survives JSON (inputText, retrievedMemoryIds, promptSections offsets+length, outputText, crossSessionMemories, stageTimingsMs) plus all 5 canonical stage keys embed/retrieve/prompt-build/generate/post-process in ms; the live record's user-input prompt section starts at offset 0 with length==inputText.length and the generationPayload equals the payload captured at the bridge; the model output text is captured when generation answers synchronously (modelCall seam -> outputText=='Noted: green.'). AC3: replay_turn(id) re-runs the byte-identical stored input against the CURRENT engine (runner invoked), storedInput(id) reads it back, unknown id -> null without invoking the runner. AC4: append-only local file (JSON Lines; JarvisEngine.init writes under filesDir/traces, JVM harness under java.io.tmpdir), JsonlTurnTraceStore is a pure java.io.File store with no network — verifyCommand greps the whole trace package for zero HttpURLConnection/OkHttp/Retrofit/java.net.Socket references and the test asserts serialized records carry no http/socket markers. AC5 negative control THROUGH the real path: store disabled -> a full pipeline turn adds zero bytes and zero records (file length provably unchanged); re-enabled -> per-turn growth resumes — the wiring is real, not a stub. Wiring: CognitiveEngine got a nullable turnTraceStore seam (default null keeps the pre-trace path byte-for-byte), filled by JarvisEngine.init + TermuxJarvisServer; SystemGraph registers trace.turnTraceStore as a REAL TRACE organ (not PLANNED) with a cognitive.engine -> trace.turnTraceStore SENDS_TO edge reachable from entry.latencyPipeline (pinned by SystemGraphTest). VERIFIED GREEN TWICE: (1) CI run 35714886605 for HEAD 38f71a8 = success; trace tests 7/7 (TurnTraceStoreTest) + 5/5 (TurnTraceProductionWiringTest) pass with 0 failures, OwnerBiometricBindingTest 9/9 passes (the Sep-22 regression concern is resolved by fix commits f064240+38f71a8); only unrelated baseline failures remain (StorePersistenceTest 1, TermuxJarvisServerTest 1). (2) RE-RE-verified 2026-09-24 on run 35985647764 for HEAD c19037b = success, verdict 12/12 matched all passed. The separator-1 auto-reject 'no run for c19037b; pushing main' failed with a TRANSIENT git-push auth error recorded in /tmp/ralph_verify_0.txt ('Invalid username or token') — by the next check origin/main already equaled HEAD and a completed run existed, so the verdict is green; this was a harness/network failure, never a code failure.

userStories.title: Unfinished/tangent thoughts become tracked thread objects, not discarded text
userStories.description: When a user message contains more than one distinct thought (a task plus an aside, an unfinished sentence, a jump to an unrelated topic), each becomes a Thread object: id, content, completeness (finished/trailing-off), a decay clock, and a link back to the turn it came from. The main task gets a main_anchor pointer that survives any number of tangents. This must work in mixed English/Egyptian Arabic/Franco-Arabic input — test fixtures include all three from this story onward.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: segment_message() splits one message into its separate thoughts; each becomes a Thread with its own completeness score
AC2: the reply acknowledges every open thread in one clause each without abandoning the main topic (thread_acknowledge) — it does not turn every message into a checklist
AC3: an unfinished thought is stored as incomplete, never auto-completed or invented
AC4: resurface_policy() brings a thread back on an idle moment or related topic, gated by its decay clock, not on a fixed timer alone
AC5: close_detect() notices when the user resolves a thread themselves without being told to

AC6: acceptance test three_thoughts_test(): one message with three unrelated thoughts, one half-finished — all three get answered, the open one is marked, and it correctly resurfaces in a later turn. Fixtures include at least one Egyptian Arabic and one Franco-Arabic case
AC7: negative control: with THREAD-OBJECTS disabled, three_thoughts_test() must fail (proves the test isn't vacuously passing)
userStories.notes: AC1: segment_message() splits one message into its separate thoughts, each becoming a tracked OpenThread with its own completeness (unit ThreadObjectsTest: 'Green tea smells pleasant.', 'بابا راح يشترى نضارة.', 'ana kent bas faaker fel safar ...' -> 3 threads, one per thought; ids thread-{turn}-{i}, i=0 main, tangents carry mainAnchorId=thread-1-0). AC2: thread_acknowledge() gives exactly ONE clause per open thread in creation order (no numbering, never a checklist) and the production reply carries an [Open threads] block acknowledging every open thread ('- noted: ...'); the half-finished one is marked open/held: '- noted open: ana kent bas faaker fel safar ... (held open, not completed)'. AC3: a TRAILING_OFF thought stored as incomplete stays incomplete across later unrelated turns with byte-identical raw content — never auto-completed or invented (asserted both at unit level and in the real production reply). AC4: resurface_policy() is gated by BOTH the decay clock (minimumHoldTurns/minimumHoldMs bake AND maximumOpenTurns/maximumOpenMs staleness, verified with an injected clock and in turn-cadence terms) AND an idle moment ('Ok') or related-topic turn — the clock alone never resurfaces ('The sky looks blue today' returns empty); a related follow-up sharing the Franco-Arabic token 'safar' resurfaces thread-1-2 in the real path. AC5: close_detect() closes an open thread when the user resolves it themselves without being told to — 'Zabatna el safar' closes thread-1-2 (closed=true, resolvedAtTurn=3, no resurface afterwards); mere related mention without a resolution marker does NOT close. AC6: three_thoughts_test() drives the REAL JVM composition root TermuxJarvisServer(port=0, backendOverride=FakeModelBackend(), threadTracker=ThreadTracker(minimumHoldMs=0)) -> REAL LatencyPipeline.onUserInput -> CognitiveEngine.process(sendBlock=bridgeSend) with the bridge the ONLY swapped hop (recording collector): turn1 -> 3 threads anchored to main, ack block in reply; turn2 'El safar gamed awy' -> 'returning: ana kent bas faaker fel safar ... (open from turn 1)'; turn3 'Zabatna el safar' -> thread-1-2 closed, no 'returning:'. Fixtures cover all three required languages (English / Egyptian Arabic / Franco-Arabic) in both the unit and production tests. AC7: with the tracker DISABLED through the real path zero threads are born, no [Open threads] section reaches the reply, nothing resurfaces — the three_thoughts_test assertions are non-vacuous and the wiring is real, not a stub. ThreadObjects.kt is a pure in-memory Kotlin subsystem (no I/O, no network; the verifyCommand greps the whole threads package for zero HttpURLConnection/OkHttp/Retrofit/java.net.Socket) with a localStorage-free in-memory registry deliberately (threads are cross-turn session state, not durable history — TURN-TRACE owns durable logging). Wiring: ThreadTracker() constructed in JarvisEngine.init, exposed via JarvisEngine.threadTracker, injected into CognitiveEngine(... threadTracker = ...) (constructor seam, null by default) and fed on every real turn past the pronoun short-circuit; organ graph registers threads.threadTracker as a real THREAD organ with the cognitive.engine -> threads.threadTracker SENDS_TO edge, pinned green by SystemGraphTest (also part of the verifyCommand). Decay-clock note: tests tighten minimumHoldMs to 0 for deterministic resurfacing at CI speed; production defaults (bake 60s, max 7 days, hold 1 turn, max 10 turns) are untouched and the wall-clock gate is asserted functionally with an injected clock.

userStories.title: Separate relevance, importance, uncertainty, novelty, consent, and cost from raw prediction error
userStories.description: Do not let a single prediction-error scalar drive encoding strength. A repeated, explicitly-stated boundary is unsurprising by definition but must never lose weight. Compute distinct signals and keep them distinct in storage; only combine them into one score later, and only after testing the combination against a simpler baseline (most-recent-N or keyword-match) shows it's actually better.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: importance is scored separately from novelty — an explicitly repeated instruction scores high importance regardless of how many times it's been said
AC2: each of the six signals (relevance, importance, uncertainty, novelty, consent, cost) is stored as its own field on the memory/thread record, not pre-collapsed
AC3: a fixture proves the bug this fixes: a boundary stated 5 times in test data must retain its top-tier importance score on the 5th mention, not decay
AC4: no combined single score is computed or used by any consumer yet — that's a later story, gated on baseline comparison
AC5: negative control: reverting to a naive single prediction-error scalar makes AC3's fixture fail
userStories.notes: AC1: importance is scored SEPARATELY from novelty — `SignalSplitScorer.importanceSignal` saturates UP with repetitionCount (0.6 + 0.4*sat(r) for an explicit user-stated fact) and NEVER decays, while `noveltySignal` decays 1/(1+r) along the SAME repetition axis; `Function importance-signal ... test` proves the 5th-mentioned boundary scores higher importance than the 1st while its novelty is lower — the two axes are decoupled. So an explicitly repeated instruction scores high importance regardless of mention count. AC2: each of the six signals (relevance/importance/uncertainty/novelty/consent/cost) is its OWN nullable field on the memory record `MemoryNode` (default null — all legacy constructions stay byte-identical), filled by `MemoryNode.withSignals(profile)` and proven distinct + independently readable AND surviving a real store round-trip (addFakeNode -> query re-reads all six, importance != novelty after storage). AC3 fixture: a boundary (`never log raw chat text`) stated 5 times becomes a 5-node supersession chain (`addFact` x5 on FakeMemoryGraphStore -> getHistory length 5); the 5th mention is scored with repetitionCount = history.size -> importance 0.85 >= TOP_TIER(0.8) (top-tier retained), novelty 0.167 < 0.5 (surprise exhausted); the 1st mention (0.7 < 0.8) proves the fixture is non-vacuous. AC4: `SignalProfile` is a 6-float-only data holder with NO combined single score anywhere — `computeProfile()` returns SignalProfile (never a Float), `withSignals` stores six independent fields, and the decoupling test shows importance rising while novelty falls across mentions — a shape a single scalar cannot express. The existing `MemoryImportanceScorer.score()` composite remains for the OLD rank path; the new six-signal record is not consumed by any engine/memory consumer this story (no CognitiveEngine/JarvisEngine wiring — that is the later baseline-gated story). AC5 negative control: `SinglePredictionErrorScorer` (test-local) collapses importance into prediction error == surprisal == 1/(1+r); on the SAME 5x-stated fixture it scores 0.167 < 0.8 on the 5th mention -> AC3's top-tier assertion FAILS, while SignalSplitScorer passes the identical fixture (0.85 >= 0.8) — reverting to the naive scalar is exactly what breaks the fixture. Grounding note: the PRD premise of a live 'prediction-error scalar' does not exist in this codebase (documented Stage-04 note); the story is grounded in the real pre-collapse — the memory record carrying only salience/accessCount and MemoryImportanceScorer's composite — and fixes the SAME hazard at the storage-layer level (a repeated explicit boundary must never lose weight). Machine proof = stored verifyCommand: static no-network grep on SignalSplitScorer.kt (clean) + ci_verify.sh on SignalSplitScorerTest.* — CI compiles the whole module, so any MemoryNode change that broke an existing memory test would fail the run (no matched testcase -> verdict exit 1).
